_findings.errexit does not apply to a `!`-inverted: THE defect class of round 21, and it invalidated three of my own fixes from the same day. bash(1) under `set -e` exempts 'any command in a pipeline but the last, or if the command's return value is being inverted with !'. So `set -e; ! grep -q x <<<x; echo REACHED` prints REACHED. Every `! grep` in these Containerfiles is written as a build-time refusal and 46 of them failed nothing — they are mid-stanza, so their status is discarded and the build only ever stops if some LATER command in the same RUN fails. Found by the p1-063 lid agent in its own stanza; it wrote its refusals as `if ... exit 1` from the start and that is the idiom adopted. Ten of the 46 are not greps and were never in reach of the resolver at all: `apex-mux nonsense-verb`, `apex vm create --graphics spice`, `apex secret --help`, `apex recover reset` as root, `command -v qemu-system-x86_64` — all carrying real security decisions and asserting nothing. esp_ownership_2026_09_21.answer: NO. Windows-side installs boot systemd-boot like every other machine, and APEX BUILDS ITS OWN ESP rather than writing into Windows'. esp_ownership_2026_09_21.why_it_is_not_a_workaround: The 512 MiB problem was never about 512 MiB, it was about BORROWING. gpt_write_policy_2026_09_21.answer: THE TOOL DOES IT. _the_thing_that_blocks_andres_merge.status: HALF FIXED BY THE PEER, HALF DISPATCHED. The keymap red is gone (peer merge 6fa9ddbc). The reason nobody saw it is dispatched as ci-selector-base.
_the_thing_that_blocks_andres_merge.the_keymap_red_and_why_the_engine_was_in: THE SUITE WAS MEASURING ITS OWN EXTRACTION. set_locale_keymap_in() calls console_keymap_for(), which calls kbd_has(); the suite extracted only the first, so both dependencies were undefined, the command substitution yielded empty, and the engine dutifully wrote a blank KEYMAP=. console_keymap_for CANNOT return empty -- step 5 falls back to us -- so an empty answer was only ever possible if the function did not exist. Fixed with both dependencies extracted PLUS a guard that refuses if the engine stops defining them, because otherwise it silently reverts to measuring nothing. 26/0, was 25/1. Also made HERMETIC rather than merely green: console_keymap_for falls back to the HOST's /usr/lib/kbd/keymaps, so adding the dependencies alone would have made the verdict depend on whether the runner has kbd installed. The fixture now carries its own tree, proven by mutation -- delete de.map.gz and the case answers us, not de.
_the_thing_that_blocks_andres_merge.MY_EARLIER_FRAMING_WAS_IMPRECISE_AND_IS_: The orchestrator reported this finding as 'a skipped job counts as success', and that is NOT the defect. pr-validation.yml's `result:` job documents that behaviour deliberately and defends it correctly: a documentation-only PR legitimately must not be blocked by the installer suite, `changes` is in `needs` so a FAILURE there is caught rather than cascading into passing skips, and `cancelled` fails too. The same comment names the real adjacent hazard and puts the remedy in the right place -- a SUITE printing '0 passed, 0 failed (skipped)' and exiting 0 is invisible to any aggregate gate, so a missing prerequisite must be a failure in the suite, never a skip.
_the_thing_that_blocks_andres_merge.the_actual_defect_read_out_of_the_file: A BASE-REF ASYMMETRY in pr-validation.yml's `changes` job. pull_request classifies against the PR base (main); push classifies against github.event.before (the branch's previous tip); workflow_dispatch classifies against `git merge-base origin/main $head`. So a push to roadmap/v2.2 sees only that push's paths while the merge PR sees the WHOLE branch diff -- the integration branch can be green on every push for weeks and red the instant it is proposed for merge. That is exactly what happened: no single push happened to touch installer/. workflow_dispatch ALREADY does the right thing ten lines away, which is the strongest argument that the push branch is an oversight rather than a decision.
_the_thing_that_blocks_andres_merge.what_is_not_yet_known: installer is ONE JOB OF FIVE. The same reasoning applies to rust, engine and android, and nobody has looked. ci-selector-base is told to re-run the full matrix on roadmap/v2.2 and REPORT what it surfaces WITHOUT fixing it -- each is its own unit, and a round that fixes five unrelated reds at once cannot say which fix did what.

_finding_alternatives_never_runs.headline: apex-pkg builds the extension by EXTRACTING RPMs, and extraction does not run %post. Every package that publishes its binaries through `alternatives` therefore installs 'successfully' into the extension AND DOES NOT WORK.
_finding_alternatives_never_runs.diagnosed_by: the peer session, landed 95c0a798. Checked against the package rather than reasoned: Fedora's wine-core OWNS /usr/bin/wine and /usr/bin/wineserver and creates them in its scriptlets via `alternatives --install`.
_finding_alternatives_never_runs.blast_radius_measured_by_the_orchestrato: EXACTLY 12 dangling symlinks in /usr/bin, all wine's, all -> wine, each 4 BYTES (the length of the string 'wine'): msidb msiexec notepad regedit regsvr32 wineboot winecfg wineconsole winedbg winefile winemine winepath. wine32/wine64/wineserver32/wineserver64 are REAL FILES, which is why wine64 --version prints wine-11.0 (Staging) and only RUNNING something fails.
_finding_alternatives_never_runs.the_calibration_that_stops_this_being_ov: **0 dangling under /etc/alternatives, and java's entries there resolve.** The IMAGE's own alternatives are fine, because the image installs by dnf and runs scriptlets. ONLY EXTENSION-INSTALLED PACKAGES ARE HIT. So the class is real but currently unrealised beyond wine on this machine -- do not write it up as 'java is broken', because on katana it is not.
_finding_alternatives_never_runs.why_it_still_deserves_a_unit: It is invisible to every cheap check: command -v answers, --version prints, ls lists the symlink happily. It surfaces only when something is RUN. Unit pkg-alternatives dispatched with the gate specified as 'the extension contains no dangling symlink that an installed package owns', provable both ways.
_finding_alternatives_never_runs.method_note: THREE CHECKS DISAGREED AND EACH WAS RIGHT ABOUT A DIFFERENT QUESTION. `ls` does not follow symlinks and listed them present; `test -e` does follow and called them missing; `stat -c %s` said 4 bytes, the length of the target string, and that is what gave it away. The mirror-image error was made earlier the same night in the other direction -- concluding wine was ABSENT from `command -v wine`, when the shipped binary is wine64. When a file's existence is the question, say WHICH existence you mean.
